key_insight: A physics-informed neural network can infer both the motion state and hydrodynamic coefficients of floating offshore structures directly from movement time-series by embedding the Cummins equations.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven way to identify added mass, damping, and restoring effects for offshore structural modeling when direct force measurements are unavailable.
method: Rewrite the Cummins equations as a first-order dynamical system.
Train a PINN using observed translational and rotational motion data plus governing physics.
Solve the inverse problem to estimate hydrodynamic parameters alongside the body state.
evidence_signal: Validated on free-decay cases for a sphere and a box, where the method accurately estimated state and coefficients using motion data.
watch_item: Estimation accuracy depends on the volume and quality of motion data, so sparse or noisy measurements may limit reliability.
paper_title: Estimating Hydrodynamic Coefficients for Floating Offshore Structures from Movement Data Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
